name: BigBlueButton
tagline: A virtual classroom: whiteboard, breakouts, polls, recordings
description: Web conferencing designed for teaching and workshops. Presenters get a multi-user whiteboard over their slides, shared notes, polls and breakout rooms; sessions are recorded on the server and play back in sync.
backing: BigBlueButton Inc. and Blindside Networks (Canada), with a large education community

maturity.rationale: Fifteen years in production at universities and schools worldwide, and integrated with Moodle, Canvas and most other learning platforms.

selfHosting.summary: It wants a dedicated Ubuntu server of one specific release with a public IP, and takes over the machine. The install script does the work, but the hardware floor is high and moving between major versions usually means a fresh server.

requirements.notes: The official minimum for production. You also need a front end to create rooms: Greenlight (included as an option) or a learning platform.

managedHosting.label: Blindside Networks
managedHosting.note: The company that leads BigBlueButton's development; hosting and support

strengths: Purpose-built for teaching: multi-user whiteboard, shared notes, polls and breakout rooms
Server-side recordings that replay slides, chat and audio together
Integrates with Moodle, Canvas, Nextcloud and Zulip
Holds up with 100 or more participants when most are listening
weaknesses: Heavy: 8 cores and 16 GB of RAM as a starting point
Overkill, and slower to start, for a quick one-to-one call
Needs a room manager (Greenlight or a learning platform) before anyone can create a meeting

featureNotes.mobile-apps: Runs in mobile browsers; no native apps
